name: Upper limb fractures
rawContent:
# Upper limb fractures: Core Condition Reference

## Overview
Upper limb fractures include bony injuries from clavicle to phalanges, commonly following falls or direct trauma.

overview.definition: Upper limb fractures include bony injuries from clavicle to phalanges, commonly following falls or direct trauma.
overview.epidemiology: Common in ED across all ages; mechanism and fracture pattern vary by age.
overview.pathophysiology: Trauma causes cortical disruption with variable displacement and neurovascular risk.

firstLine: X-rays including joint above and below

diagnosis.criteria: Confirmed radiologically with clinical correlation and neurovascular assessment.

firstLine: Open fracture protocol (IV antibiotics/tetanus per policy)
Early orthopaedic discussion for displaced/unstable injuries
secondLine: Manipulation/reduction under appropriate analgesia/sedation if indicated
procedures: Operative fixation for unstable, displaced, intra-articular, or open fractures

monitoring: Fracture clinic follow-up, repeat imaging, physiotherapy and functional rehabilitation

content.prognosis: Most heal with appropriate immobilisation or fixation, though stiffness and functional deficits may persist.
content.foundationDoctorRole: Provide initial trauma assessment, analgesia, immobilisation, and clear neurovascular documentation.
content.escalation: Escalate immediately for open injury, absent pulses, progressive pain, paraesthesia, or threatened skin.
content.keySafetyConsiderations: Repeat neurovascular exams after any manipulation/splinting and before discharge.
